your-first-pack.title: Your first pack
your-first-pack.markdown:
## Before you start
You need Minecraft Java Edition, a text editor, and a Citadel server you
can run or edit. On your own machine, the commands below assume the
`citadel` executable is on your `PATH`. If you built it from source, use
the path to `target/release/citadel` instead.
A **pack** is a folder containing configuration and Luau scripts. Citadel
runs those scripts on the server; players join with their normal Minecraft
client. You do not need to compile the scripts or install a client mod.
This guide uses **lite mode**, where your pack supplies the world and the
game’s behaviour. By the end, a player will spawn on a gold block, see a
welcome, and be able to walk away and return with `/spawn`.
## 1. Create the two files
Make a folder named `first`. Inside it, create these two files:
```text
first/
  citadel.yml
  main.luau
```
Put this in `citadel.yml`:
```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: first
entry: main.luau
motd: My first Citadel pack
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
```
| Setting | What it does here |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Names this pack `first`. |
| `entry` | Tells Citadel to run `main.luau` when the pack loads. |
| `motd` | Sets the description shown in Minecraft’s server list. |
| `spawn_point` | Places a joining player’s feet at x = 0.5, y = 65, z = 0.5. |
| `gamemode: 2` | Uses adventure mode, so players can explore without breaking the floor. |
| `mode: lite` | Selects a game controlled by your scripts. |
| `world: script` | Asks your script to generate the terrain. |
This is the **pack’s** `citadel.yml`. A separate `citadel.yml` in the
directory where you start the server configures things such as its port.
Keep the pack inside `first`, and run the local commands below from the
directory containing `first`.
Start `main.luau` with `--!strict`. This enables strict checking in an
editor configured with Citadel’s `citadel.d.luau` type definitions. The
pack can run without that editor setup.
## 2. Give players ground to stand on
Add this below `--!strict` in `main.luau`:
```luau
-- main.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(
        vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z),
        vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z),
        "stone"
    )
    chunk:set(vec3(0, 64, 0), "gold_block")
end)
```
Minecraft divides the world into **chunks**, each 16 blocks wide and 16
blocks deep. `world.on_generate` registers a function that Citadel calls
when it needs a chunk’s terrain. The `chunk` argument is the chunk being
built.
`vec3(x, y, z)` describes a position: x and z are horizontal; y is height.
`chunk:fill` fills the box between two corners, including both corners.
Using the chunk’s x and z bounds and y = 64 for both corners makes a stone
floor one block thick. Every generated chunk gets that floor.
`chunk:set` replaces one floor block with gold. It ignores coordinates
outside the current chunk, so only the chunk containing `(0, 64, 0)` gets
the marker. The spawn point is one block above it; the `.5` coordinates
place the player in the centre of the block.
Keep terrain generation repeatable: the same chunk should receive the same
blocks each time the function is called.
## 3. Run the pack and join
From the directory containing `first`, run:
```sh
citadel --lite --pack ./first
```
Leave that terminal open. In Minecraft, choose **Multiplayer → Direct
Connection**, enter `localhost:25565`, and join. If your server uses a
different port, use that port instead.
On a hosted Minefort server, put the `first` folder in the server’s `packs`
directory, select lite mode, and start the server. Join using the address
shown for that server.
**Check:** you should stand on a gold block surrounded by a flat stone
floor. Walk a few blocks and look back at the marker. There is no welcome
message or `/spawn` command yet; you will add those next.
## 4. Welcome each player
Append this after the terrain code:
```luau
-- main.luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{
        title = "Welcome",
        subtitle = player.name,
        color = "aqua",
    }
    player:message("Walk around, then type /spawn to return to the gold block.", "aqua")
end)
```
`players.on_join` registers another function, this time for a player joining.
Citadel passes that player into the function as `player`. `player.name`
reads their name; `player.ui.title` shows them a title; `player:message`
sends them a chat message. These calls address that one player.
The code inside the function runs when the event happens. Register the
function once at the top level of the script; you do not need a loop that
keeps checking for new players.
Save `main.luau` while connected. Citadel reloads the script and runs its
join callbacks for players already online too.
**Check:** a “Welcome” title should appear with your name underneath it,
and chat should explain `/spawn`. That command is the next step.
## 5. Add a command that does something
Append this below the welcome code:
```luau
-- main.luau
commands.add("spawn", function(player)
    player:teleport(world.spawn_point)
    player:message("You are back at spawn.", "green")
end, { help = "Return to the lobby spawn" })
```
`commands.add` registers the name `"spawn"` without the slash. When a player
types `/spawn`, Citadel calls the function with the player who used it.
The `help` text describes the command.
`world.spawn_point` reads the spawn configured in `citadel.yml`, so you do
not need to repeat its coordinates in the script. `player:teleport` moves
the player there, and the message confirms the action.
Notice the colon in `player:teleport(...)` and `chunk:fill(...)`: these are
methods acting on a particular player or chunk. Namespace functions such
as `commands.add(...)` and `player.ui.title(...)` use a dot. Follow the
signature shown in the reference when using a new API.
**Check:** save, walk away from the gold block, and type `/spawn`. You
should return to the marker and see “You are back at spawn.” in chat.
## 6. Make a change and check it
Change `title = "Welcome"` to `title = "My lobby"`, then save. The new title
should appear without disconnecting you. Try `/spawn` again to confirm the
rest of the pack still works.
A script reload keeps the existing world. Changing the floor in
`world.on_generate` affects newly generated chunks; it does not repaint the
stone already around you. Restart after changing the pack manifest.
If a step does not work, check the server log first:
| What you see | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| The server cannot find the pack | Run from the directory containing `first`, or pass the full folder path to `--pack`. |
| You cannot connect | Keep the server running and use its configured address and port. |
| There is no floor | Check `world: script`, the `entry` filename, and any error reported while loading `main.luau`. |
| `/spawn` is unknown | Check that you saved the command block in the loaded pack and that the script reloaded successfully. |
| An edit does not take effect | Look for a filename and line number in the log. If loading the new script fails, Citadel keeps the previous working script. |
## The complete script
Your final `main.luau` should look like this. Use it to compare with your
file, or replace the file with it; do not append a second copy.
```luau
-- main.luau
--!strict
-- A small lobby: solid ground, a welcome, and a way back to spawn.

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(
        vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z),
        vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z),
        "stone"
    )
    chunk:set(vec3(0, 64, 0), "gold_block")
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{
        title = "Welcome",
        subtitle = player.name,
        color = "aqua",
    }
    player:message("Walk around, then type /spawn to return to the gold block.", "aqua")
end)

commands.add("spawn", function(player)
    player:teleport(world.spawn_point)
    player:message("You are back at spawn.", "green")
end, { help = "Return to the lobby spawn" })
```
You have used three entry points: terrain generation for the world,
`players.on_join` for a player’s arrival, and `commands.add` for an action
the player chooses.
## Try this next
- Change the welcome text and its colour, save, and check the result.
- Add a `/hello` command that sends a message to the player who uses it.
- Add another gold marker in the terrain function, then look for it in a
newly generated chunk.
Continue with **Coin rush** to add an objective, a score, and repeating
rounds. It builds on the pack structure and event callbacks you used here.

client-versions.title: Client versions
client-versions.markdown:
```luau
if player:supports("display") then
    world.display{ kind = "text", text = "Bet 50", at = pad }
else
    board:text(8, 8, "Bet 50", colors.white, 24)   -- a screen works from 1.8
end
```
| feature | what needs it | from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bossbar` | `ui.bossbar`, `player.ui.bossbar` | 1.9 |
| `potion_color` | an item’s `color` | 1.11 |
| `floor_frame` | a screen or frame with `facing = "up"` | 1.13 |
| `light` | `world.light` | 1.14 |
| `hex_color` | a colour outside Minecraft’s sixteen names | 1.16 |
| `glow_frame` | `glow = true` on a screen | 1.17 |
| `display` | `world.display`, any kind | 1.19.4 |
| `hitbox` | `world.hitbox` | 1.19.4 |
| `model` | `world.display{ kind = "model" }` | 1.21.4 |
| `layout` | `player.ui.show` | 1.21.4 |
| `dialog` | `player.ui.dialog` | 1.21.6 |
| `overlay` | `player.ui.overlay` | 26.3 only |
| `resource_pack` | the pack’s textures, models and sounds | a client that did not turn the pack down |
- A name not in this table is an error.
- A client that turns the resource pack down answers false to
`resource_pack`, `model`, `layout`, `dialog` and `overlay`, from the
moment it answers. It is sent no layout and no dialog: they are drawn in
the pack’s fonts. An open dialog closes.
- A Bedrock client answers false to every feature in this table.
- Unguarded calls are safe: a client that cannot show a feature is not
sent it. Guard only to show something else.
- Or set `min_client` in `citadel.yml` to refuse old clients.

packs.title: Packs
packs.markdown:
The script runs on every Java client from 1.8 to 26.2 and never sees a
client version. To check a feature, ask `player:supports` (see “Client
versions”).
`packs/citadel.d.luau` types this whole API. Start a script with `--!strict`
and point a language server at that file to catch misspelt fields.
Use the standard platform and Luau’s new type solver (luau-lsp 1.70.1 or
later). For a command-line check:
```sh
luau-lsp analyze --platform=standard --flag:LuauSolverV2=true --definitions=packs/citadel.d.luau main.luau
```
In VS Code, set `luau-lsp.platform.type` to `standard`, add the definitions
file to `luau-lsp.types.definitionFiles`, and set
`luau-lsp.fflags.override` to `{ "LuauSolverV2": "true" }`.
citadel.yml
Run it: `citadel --lite --pack ./rave`.
## Loading
- The entry script has **5 s** of work between two waits (`task.wait`), and
30 s in all. Past that, the load fails and the log says why.
- Build big scenery once at load and copy it, for example one tree variant
pasted per chunk. Do not loop over every block of every level at load.
## Textures of your own
On Java 1.21.4 and later, a pack’s own items and blocks can have textures.
Set `texture` in `game.items.define` and `game.blocks.define` (below). The
engine adds them to its resource pack. Older clients see the vanilla item or
block. A client that turns the resource pack down sees them too from then on
(`player:supports("resource_pack")` is false). A pack that needs the textures
says so:
Every other folder in `<pack>/assets/` (not `sounds`) goes into the resource
pack unchanged (`assets/<pack>/textures/...`).
## Mode
`mode` says **who owns the game**. In a pack manifest, it names the kind of
server the pack is *for*.
- `mode: lite`: your scripts are the game.
- `mode: full`: **Citadel plays survival** (terrain, health, hunger, mining,
inventory, mobs, world rules). A pack cannot ship survival; it *adds* to
it (a shop, a scoreboard, a custom drop).
- **no `mode` key**: the pack runs on either kind of server, like a plugin.
`citadel` with no flags (or `--full`) runs survival with `gamemode: 0` and
the overworld. `--lite` makes the packs own the game. Add packs to either
with `--pack ./shop` or `--packs-dir ./packs`.
- A `--lite` server with no packs does not start survival. It runs with an
empty world and no game, and the log says so. Add a pack and restart.
- With no flag and no server file, the packs’ manifests decide. Packs that
name different modes, or that all name none, stop the server. The message
says how to set one.
- A flag or the server file overrules a pack that names the other mode. The
log names that pack.

BarColor.title: BarColor type
BarColor.lead: A boss bar's colour is its own closed set — six the client draws, and anything else is white. It is not an `Ink`: the bar has no hex form.

World.title: world global · type World
World.lead: A room's blocks, entities, displays, screens and time: the `world` global, or `room.world`.

members.name: on_generate
members.signature: world.on_generate(fn: (chunk: Chunk) -> ())
members.description: Called for a chunk each time it comes into memory, in a script world; it must make the same blocks every time.

members.name: on_populate
members.signature: world.on_populate(fn: (chunk: Chunk) -> ())
members.description: Each chunk the overworld terrain made, once, after it made it.

members.name: dimension
members.signature: world.dimension(name: string) → World
members.description: Another world of the server's group, by dimension id or its last part ("dungeon", "minecraft:the_nether"): that world's own `world` table.

members.name: drop
members.signature: world.drop(pos: Vec3, item: ItemSpec)
members.description: A stack on the ground at a block, as a broken block leaves one.

members.name: container
members.signature: world.container(pos: Vec3) → Container ?
members.description: A chest's stacks, or nil where the block keeps none.

members.name: rules
members.signature: world.rules(opts: { survival: boolean ?, fall: boolean ?, damage: boolean ?, hunger: boolean ?, anticheat: boolean ?, day_cycle: boolean ?, redstone: boolean ? }?) → Rules
members.description: `world.rules{ fall = true }` switches one on, false off; a rule left out or nil keeps its value, and a number or a string is an error. `world.rules()` reads them.

members.name: raycast
members.signature: world.raycast(from: Vec3, direction: Vec3, max: number ?) → RayHit ?
members.description: The first block a ray from `from` along `direction` meets within `max` blocks, and the face it came in through; nil for none.

members.name: sees
members.signature: world.sees(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) → boolean
members.description: True when no block stops the line from `from` to `to`: a block with a collision box does (glass, leaves), water and grass do not.

members.name: raycasts
members.signature: world.raycasts(rays: buffer, out: buffer, n: number)
members.description: `n` lines at once. `rays` holds six f64 a line (from x, y, z, to x, y, z); `out` gets one f64 a line: how far along it the first block is that stops it, or -1 for a clear line.

members.name: light_at
members.signature: world.light_at(pos: Vec3) → (number, number, boolean)
members.description: Block light and sky light, 0 to 15, and whether nothing above holds off the sky.

members.name: path
members.signature: world.path(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, opts: { size: (number | { number })?, swim: boolean ?, fall: number ?, range: number ?, budget: number ? }?) → { Vec3 }?
members.description: The points a body walks from `from` to the block at `to`, or nil. The game's own search: a step up of one block, falls of `fall` (3). `size` is { width, height } (0.6, 1.8); `swim` goes through water; `range` (the distance + 16) and `budget` (2000 nodes) stop a long search, which then gives the part that came closest.

members.name: zone
members.signature: world.zone(opts: { from: Vec3, to: Vec3, on_enter: ((player: Player) -> ())?, on_leave: ((player: Player) -> ())? }) → Zone
members.description: Makes a box of blocks, both corners included, that knows who is in it; checked once a tick by feet position. Ends with the script.

members.name: set_block
members.signature: world.set_block(pos: Vec3, block: BlockRef, opts: { skin: HeadSkin ? }?)
members.description: `skin` is for "player_head" and "player_wall_head" only: an account's name, or the raw `textures` property.

members.name: set_blocks
members.signature: world.set_blocks(changes: { { at: Vec3, block: BlockRef, skin: HeadSkin ? } })
members.description: Sets many blocks at once, live, stored and sent; the cheapest way. A row takes `skin` too, for a player head.

members.name: fill
members.signature: world.fill(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: BlockRef)
members.description: Fills a box of blocks between two corners, live, stored and sent to everyone.

members.name: schematic
members.signature: world.schematic(file: string) → Schematic
members.description: A file inside the pack; a path that leaves it, or one that is not there, is an error naming the file.

members.name: build
members.signature: world.build(fn: (b: Builder) -> (), opts: { detail: number ? }?) → Schematic
members.description: The same value, written in code instead of read from a file. `{ detail = 2 }`: coordinates are half blocks, fitted to slabs and stairs.

members.name: paste
members.signature: world.paste(schem: Schematic, origin: Vec3, opts: { air: boolean ?, part: string ? }?)
members.description: Live, stored and sent; air is skipped unless `air` is true.

members.name: get_block
members.signature: world.get_block(pos: Vec3) → string ?
members.description: `nil` where that chunk is not in memory: a read never generates.

members.name: block
members.signature: world.block(pos: Vec3) → BlockAt ?
members.description: The block there as the handle a hook gets: reads are live, and what it does lands on the next tick. `state` and `data` are for this pack's own blocks. `nil` where that chunk is not in memory.

members.name: get_biome
members.signature: world.get_biome(pos: Vec3) → string ?
members.description: Returns the biome name of the column at `pos`; `nil` where that chunk is not in memory.

members.name: generate
members.signature: world.generate(rules: GeneratorRules) → Generated
members.description: Declares this world: the engine makes each chunk from the rules, on every core, and no script runs for a chunk.

members.name: get_blocks
members.signature: world.get_blocks(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) → { string ? }
members.description: A box, in x, then z, then y order.

members.name: items
members.signature: world.items() → { GroundItem }
members.description: The stacks on the ground: `{ id, item, count, at }` rows.

members.name: spawn
members.signature: world.spawn(def: EntityDef | string, pos: Vec3, data: { [string]: any }?) → EntityHandle ?
members.description: Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have.

members.name: entities
members.signature: world.entities(query: { near: Vec3 ?, radius: number ?, kind: string ?, mob: boolean ? }?) → { EntityHandle }
members.description: Live and queued entities, in ascending id. Optional near/radius select a sphere; kind filters by canonical name. near and radius go together. `mob = true` gives the mobs only, `mob = false` the rest.

members.name: explode
members.signature: world.explode(pos: Vec3, power: number ?)
members.description: A blast at a point. The power is clamped by this game's own column and the tick's explosion budget decides when it goes off, never whether.

members.name: on_block_break
members.signature: world.on_block_break(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: What the survival tick did. Observe-only: the world has already changed, and what the callback returns is not read.

members.name: on_block_place
members.signature: world.on_block_place(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a block was placed, with its canonical name. Observe-only; `player` is nil when nobody placed it or they left.

members.name: on_entity_spawn
members.signature: world.on_entity_spawn(fn: (entity: EntityHandle, name: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a mob appeared, with its handle and name; a natural spawn fires it on every game version that has one, and a pack's own `world.spawn("cow", pos)` fires it too. Mob kinds only.

members.name: on_entity_death
members.signature: world.on_entity_death(fn: (id: number, name: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a mob died; it is gone, so its id and name is all there is. Mob kinds only.

members.name: time
members.signature: world.time((at: number | TimeName | (s: number) -> number | TimeName) -> ()) → & (() -> number)
members.description: Holds the sky at a time (ticks, or "sunrise", "day", "noon", "sunset", "night", "midnight"), or asks a function each tick, `s` seconds after the call. With no argument: the time of day now, 0 to 23999.

members.name: light
members.signature: world.light(sources: { LightSource })
members.description: Sends players light no block makes, 1 to 15 a source; each call replaces the last, `{}` ends it. 1.14 and later.

members.name: screen
members.signature: world.screen(opts: { at: Vec3, facing: Facing | "up", up: Facing ?, width: number ?, height: number ?, glow: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, x: number, y: number, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Screen
members.description: Puts a wall of map frames, `width` by `height` frames (128 pixels each), in front of a wall; `at` is the top-left frame. Returns a Screen.

members.name: canvas
members.signature: world.canvas(opts: { width: number ?, height: number ? }?) → Canvas
members.description: Makes a picture of `width` by `height` maps (1 by 1 by default, 16 at most a side) with no frame of its own, for a frame, a hand or a screen.

members.name: display
members.signature: world.display((opts: { kind: "model", model: Model, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (number | Vec3)?, -- models require equal positive axes paint: { [string]: Ink }?, fallback: string ?, seats: { Vec3 }?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> ModelDisplay) → & ((opts: { kind: "item" | "text" | "block" | "frame", at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (Vec3 | number)?, billboard: Billboard ?, glow: (Ink | false)?, item: ItemSpec ?, canvas: Canvas ?, context: Context ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: (Ink | false)?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, block: string ?, facing: ScreenFacing ?, invisible: boolean ?, glide: number ?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> Display)
members.description: A model stands in the world through the same call as everything else, and is the one kind that hands back something other than a Display.

members.name: hitbox
members.signature: world.hitbox(opts: { at: Vec3, width: number ?, height: number ?, depth: number ?, solid: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Hitbox
members.description: Makes an invisible box a player can click; `solid` also makes it a wall. `depth` is the width unless given. 1.19.4 and later.

members.name: npc
members.signature: world.npc(opts: { name: string ?, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: BodyRotation ?, skin: (string | { value: string, signature: string } | false)?, }) → Npc
members.description: Places a player-shaped entity every client from 1.8 sees; removed when the script ends or reloads.

members.name: puppet
members.signature: world.puppet(opts: { kind: string, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: BodyRotation ?, name: Text ? }) → Puppet
members.description: Places a mob's body with no mind of its own that the script moves; its name tag always shows. An error when this game has no such mob kind.

members.signature: world.spawn_point: Vec3
members.description: Where players arrive in this room; writable. The same value as the room's `spawn_point`.

members.name: light_at
members.signature: world.light_at(pos: Vec3) → (number, number, boolean)
members.description: Block light and sky light, 0 to 15, and whether nothing above holds off the sky.

members.name: path
members.signature: world.path(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, opts: { size: (number | { number })?, swim: boolean ?, fall: number ?, range: number ?, budget: number ? }?) → { Vec3 }?
members.description: The points a body walks from `from` to the block at `to`, or nil. The game's own search: a step up of one block, falls of `fall` (3). `size` is { width, height } (0.6, 1.8); `swim` goes through water; `range` (the distance + 16) and `budget` (2000 nodes) stop a long search, which then gives the part that came closest.

members.name: zone
members.signature: world.zone(opts: { from: Vec3, to: Vec3, on_enter: ((player: Player) -> ())?, on_leave: ((player: Player) -> ())? }) → Zone
members.description: Makes a box of blocks, both corners included, that knows who is in it; checked once a tick by feet position. Ends with the script.

members.name: set_block
members.signature: world.set_block(pos: Vec3, block: BlockRef, opts: { skin: HeadSkin ? }?)
members.description: `skin` is for "player_head" and "player_wall_head" only: an account's name, or the raw `textures` property.

members.name: set_blocks
members.signature: world.set_blocks(changes: { { at: Vec3, block: BlockRef, skin: HeadSkin ? } })
members.description: Sets many blocks at once, live, stored and sent; the cheapest way. A row takes `skin` too, for a player head.

members.name: fill
members.signature: world.fill(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: BlockRef)
members.description: Fills a box of blocks between two corners, live, stored and sent to everyone.

members.name: schematic
members.signature: world.schematic(file: string) → Schematic
members.description: A file inside the pack; a path that leaves it, or one that is not there, is an error naming the file.

members.name: build
members.signature: world.build(fn: (b: Builder) -> (), opts: { detail: number ? }?) → Schematic
members.description: The same value, written in code instead of read from a file. `{ detail = 2 }`: coordinates are half blocks, fitted to slabs and stairs.

members.name: paste
members.signature: world.paste(schem: Schematic, origin: Vec3, opts: { air: boolean ?, part: string ? }?)
members.description: Live, stored and sent; air is skipped unless `air` is true.

members.name: get_block
members.signature: world.get_block(pos: Vec3) → string ?
members.description: `nil` where that chunk is not in memory: a read never generates.

members.name: block
members.signature: world.block(pos: Vec3) → BlockAt ?
members.description: The block there as the handle a hook gets: reads are live, and what it does lands on the next tick. `state` and `data` are for this pack's own blocks. `nil` where that chunk is not in memory.

members.name: get_biome
members.signature: world.get_biome(pos: Vec3) → string ?
members.description: Returns the biome name of the column at `pos`; `nil` where that chunk is not in memory.

members.name: generate
members.signature: world.generate(rules: GeneratorRules) → Generated
members.description: Declares this world: the engine makes each chunk from the rules, on every core, and no script runs for a chunk.

members.name: get_blocks
members.signature: world.get_blocks(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) → { string ? }
members.description: A box, in x, then z, then y order.

members.name: items
members.signature: world.items() → { GroundItem }
members.description: The stacks on the ground: `{ id, item, count, at }` rows.

members.name: spawn
members.signature: world.spawn(def: EntityDef | string, pos: Vec3, data: { [string]: any }?) → EntityHandle ?
members.description: Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have.

members.name: entities
members.signature: world.entities(query: { near: Vec3 ?, radius: number ?, kind: string ?, mob: boolean ? }?) → { EntityHandle }
members.description: Live and queued entities, in ascending id. Optional near/radius select a sphere; kind filters by canonical name. near and radius go together. `mob = true` gives the mobs only, `mob = false` the rest.

members.name: explode
members.signature: world.explode(pos: Vec3, power: number ?)
members.description: A blast at a point. The power is clamped by this game's own column and the tick's explosion budget decides when it goes off, never whether.

members.name: on_block_break
members.signature: world.on_block_break(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: What the survival tick did. Observe-only: the world has already changed, and what the callback returns is not read.

members.name: on_block_place
members.signature: world.on_block_place(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a block was placed, with its canonical name. Observe-only; `player` is nil when nobody placed it or they left.

members.name: on_entity_spawn
members.signature: world.on_entity_spawn(fn: (entity: EntityHandle, name: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a mob appeared, with its handle and name; a natural spawn fires it on every game version that has one, and a pack's own `world.spawn("cow", pos)` fires it too. Mob kinds only.

members.name: on_entity_death
members.signature: world.on_entity_death(fn: (id: number, name: string) -> ()) → Connection
members.description: Tells after a mob died; it is gone, so its id and name is all there is. Mob kinds only.

members.name: time
members.signature: world.time((at: number | TimeName | (s: number) -> number | TimeName) -> ()) → & (() -> number)
members.description: Holds the sky at a time (ticks, or "sunrise", "day", "noon", "sunset", "night", "midnight"), or asks a function each tick, `s` seconds after the call. With no argument: the time of day now, 0 to 23999.

members.name: light
members.signature: world.light(sources: { LightSource })
members.description: Sends players light no block makes, 1 to 15 a source; each call replaces the last, `{}` ends it. 1.14 and later.

members.name: screen
members.signature: world.screen(opts: { at: Vec3, facing: Facing | "up", up: Facing ?, width: number ?, height: number ?, glow: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, x: number, y: number, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Screen
members.description: Puts a wall of map frames, `width` by `height` frames (128 pixels each), in front of a wall; `at` is the top-left frame. Returns a Screen.

members.name: canvas
members.signature: world.canvas(opts: { width: number ?, height: number ? }?) → Canvas
members.description: Makes a picture of `width` by `height` maps (1 by 1 by default, 16 at most a side) with no frame of its own, for a frame, a hand or a screen.

members.name: display
members.signature: world.display((opts: { kind: "model", model: Model, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (number | Vec3)?, -- models require equal positive axes paint: { [string]: Ink }?, fallback: string ?, seats: { Vec3 }?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> ModelDisplay) → & ((opts: { kind: "item" | "text" | "block" | "frame", at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (Vec3 | number)?, billboard: Billboard ?, glow: (Ink | false)?, item: ItemSpec ?, canvas: Canvas ?, context: Context ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: (Ink | false)?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, block: string ?, facing: ScreenFacing ?, invisible: boolean ?, glide: number ?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> Display)
members.description: A model stands in the world through the same call as everything else, and is the one kind that hands back something other than a Display.

members.name: hitbox
members.signature: world.hitbox(opts: { at: Vec3, width: number ?, height: number ?, depth: number ?, solid: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Hitbox
members.description: Makes an invisible box a player can click; `solid` also makes it a wall. `depth` is the width unless given. 1.19.4 and later.

members.name: npc
members.signature: world.npc(opts: { name: string ?, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: BodyRotation ?, skin: (string | { value: string, signature: string } | false)?, }) → Npc
members.description: Places a player-shaped entity every client from 1.8 sees; removed when the script ends or reloads.

members.name: puppet
members.signature: world.puppet(opts: { kind: string, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: BodyRotation ?, name: Text ? }) → Puppet
members.description: Places a mob's body with no mind of its own that the script moves; its name tag always shows. An error when this game has no such mob kind.

members.name: spawn_point
members.signature: world.spawn_point: Vec3
members.description: Where players arrive in this room; writable. The same value as the room's `spawn_point`.

max_health.title: player.max_health
max_health.lead: Their health now, 0 to `max_health`; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable: set outright, no flash; 0 is a death; a number above `max_health` stops there. The most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable, 1 to 1024; nil gives the game's own back. A lower maximum takes `health` down to it. It lasts for the session. Every Java client draws its hearts; Bedrock draws none.

used_in.quote: player.health          -- their health now, 0 to player.max_health; nil where the version has no damage rules
player.max_health      -- the most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it; nil for the same reason
player.health = 20             -- set outright, no flash; 0 is a death; above player.max_health it stops there

message.title: player:message
message.lead: What shows on this player's screen: the calls `ui` has, for them alone, plus their own menu and overlay. Sends a chat line to this player alone; `color` is for the words that did not pick one. Chat is not part of the screen, so it is not in `ui`.

reads their name; `player.ui.title` shows them a title; `player:message`
